newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly firmer.

text.p: COMEX copper was called to open slightly firmer on Tuesday amid reports that operations at strike-hit Escondida mine in Chile are being affected, and of a further draw in LME stocks.
The cash to three months backwardation on LME firmed again overnight, up some $20 to $60/$65 following a similar strengthening on Monday.
LME stocks fell 1,875 tonnes to 150,125 tonnes Tuesday.
COMEX copper stocks rose 1,697 short tons to 48,763 short tons Friday.
COMEX May copper was seen opening up 0.20 to 0.50 cent per pound from Monday's settlement at 107.20 cents, after trading between 108.00 to 106.70 cents in overnight ACCESS trade.

Management at Escondida said late Monday that 350 people were now on strike and the mine was operating at 85 percent of normal rate. Production of concentrates and cathodes were at normal levels, management added.
